payload.title: What Are the Armenian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Armenian wedding traditions in the order families live them, from the formal asking and the godparents to the church crowning, lavash at the door and Kochari, plus the travel advice and legal steps for marrying in Armenia.
payload.author: Wedded Wonderland
key_takeaways: Parishes describe the church crowning as the high point of an Armenian Apostolic wedding, and the couple share a blessed cup as a sign they will share everything in life.

UNESCO records that lavash is placed on newlyweds' shoulders for fertility and prosperity, and the Smithsonian describes the couple being offered honey and breaking plates before they enter the groom's house.
Kochari, the group dance UNESCO lists as performed at holidays, festive celebrations and family ceremonies, is open to everyone whatever their age.
Smartraveller rates Armenia Level 2 overall and Level 4 within 5 km of the Azerbaijan border, and Australia's consular help for Armenia comes from Moscow.

faq.a: There is no fixed length. The Smithsonian's curator noted that each region of Armenia has its own wedding style. Some families spread the asking, engagement, crowning and reception across weeks or months; others hold them within a day or two.

faq.q: What happens at an Armenian church wedding?
faq.a: Parishes describe the joining of right hands, the blessing and exchange of rings, the crowning of the couple as king and queen of their home, and a shared cup of blessed wine, closing with a benediction. Ask your priest, as practice can vary.

faq.q: What is the lavash tradition at Armenian weddings?
faq.a: UNESCO records that lavash is placed on the shoulders of newlyweds to bring fertility and prosperity; in the Smithsonian's account, the mother-in-law lays it there.

faq.q: Is a church wedding in Armenia legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: We cannot give a general answer, and this is not legal advice. Check with Armenia's civil registry and the Armenian embassy, including any fees, whether a church wedding alone is legally valid there, and read our guide on registering an overseas marriage at home.
